items.title: Keep geopolitics out of marine science
items.description: The politicization of marine scientific research is undermining the very cooperation needed to protect the oceans. Recently, some Philippine commentators have portrayed China's marine research activities near Huangyan Island and elsewhere in the South China Sea as potential "military threats". They have coined the term "ghost research ships", suggesting that routine scientific work is linked to military operations, submarine navigation and even anti-submarine warfare. By intertwining technological possibilities, the sensitivity of the locations and existing geopolitical tensions, they have crafted a narrative that misrepresents China's marine research as a "security concern". These claims lack supporting evidence and run counter to the international community's shared interest in advancing ocean science and protecting the marine environment.

items.title: HK building a safer future for residents after Wang Fuk Court fire
items.description: In response to the Wang Fuk Court fire, Hong Kong is taking decisive steps to ensure the safety of its residents. The government's response has been extensive, going beyond the resignation of a minister. It has provided support for displaced families, pursued legal action against those responsible and initiated significant changes in the oversight of building maintenance. The safety of the residents is at the center of these reforms.
